bindings.label: Persistent ulcer on the anterior left shin with left leg pain for 15 days, recurring over the past 4 years
An 8-year-old girl from a rural area had symptoms recurring over 4 years; the ulcer usually healed with antibiotics but reappeared after a few days.
Physical examination revealed a 3 × 3 cm ulcer on the anterior shin and a healed ulcer just above it; sensation was intact, with no thickened nerves or lymphadenopathy.
Biopsy of the ulcer showed chronic inflammatory infiltrate; imaging showed no signs of osteomyelitis; general, systemic, and laboratory investigations were within normal limits.
The patient received anti-tubercular therapy followed by multidrug therapy for leprosy, but the ulcer continued to recur.
Wound culture, special stains, and PCR results are unavailable
Autoimmune serology and direct immunofluorescence (DIF) results are unavailable

Laboratory physician analysis: the ulcer's temporary response to antibiotics and chronic inflammatory infiltrate fit a chronic bacterial ulcer, but wound culture, 16S PCR, and special stains are still needed to confirm it and rule out autoimmune ulcer.
